summary: Fulton County tower in Buchanan State Forest: 60-foot steel tower erected 1923, staffed in 1971. No source read gives its later fate or what remains on the hill.

facts.design: Sixty-foot steel tower, erected by the state Department of Forests and Waters

events.note: C. R. Meek, Assistant Chief of the Bureau of Forest Protection, inspected the proposed site for a new fire observation tower on Sideling Hill
Sixty-foot steel tower erected on the site to detect and report forest fires
Notice places the tower on Ball Hill, reached from the top of Sideling Hill, about a mile from the highway; as many as forty visitors came in one day
Notice says a beacon light would be installed and maintained by the lighthouse service to guide aviators on the Washington to Cleveland mail route
Anna May Mellott, who had worked the Tuscarora tower, was promoted to Sideling Hill that year

sources.title: Sideling Hill - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting The Fulton Democrat, 1922; Huntingdon Daily News, 1924; The Altoona Mirror, 1930; Public Opinion, 1971)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1924 notice places the tower on Ball Hill, reached from the top of Sideling Hill; the 1922 and 1930 notices both name Sideling Hill, and the story uses that name.

notes_for_editor: Single source: one transcribed-newspaper page. No fate and no present-day site description was found in any page read, so the story says so. LEAD, NOT IN STORY: 2026 press releases (Gant News, 21 Sep 2026, https://gantnews.com/2026/09/21/restored-fire-tower-now-stands-at-pennsylvania-lumber-museum/; Courier Express, https://www.thecourierexpress.com/news/state/restored-fire-tower-now-stands-at-pennsylvania-lumber-museum/article_b53b95b2-f361-4cda-b088-d91f08b1f9f1.html) say the Lumber Heritage Region and PALMA restored a reclaimed fire tower now at the Pennsylvania Lumber Museum, 5660 U.S. Route 6 West, Ulysses (Potter County). The releases do not name its origin. A Bradford Era report of 3 Sep 2026 (https://www.bradfordera.com/2026/09/03/pennsylvania-lumber-museum-restores-historic-fire-tower/) and museum and group posts appear in search snippets to name Sideling Hill as the origin, with sections received in 2022. Those texts could not be read (Bradford gave only a teaser, Facebook a login wall, PressReader a 403), so the move is not in the story. Confirm before publishing; if confirmed, add a relocation paragraph, status moved, and events for the 2022 removal and 2026 re-erection. Build-year conflict to resolve then: museum snippets say 1922 and Blaw Knox; the 1930 notice says 1923, which the story follows. Agency omitted: the 1930 notice names the department, but no current agency was found. Reads: 7 page fetches (one 403, one login wall) against a cap of 6, to try to confirm the origin; 2 searches.
